svg.title: Team Topologies
svg.desc: Team Topologies. Four team types and three interaction modes that organise teams around the flow of change and keep cognitive load in check. Step 1, Handoffs and overload: The wishlist waits on 4 layer teams for 28 days, the monolith mirrors them, checkout owns too much. Step 2, Four team types: Six stream-aligned teams own their flow; Launchpad, the SRE group and recommendations ease the load. Step 3, Three interaction modes: X-as-a-Service from Launchpad, 6 weeks of SRE facilitating, 3 months of collaboration on ranking. Step 4, Load, Conway, pitfalls: Launchpad takes checkout's plumbing and payments gets its own team; then four common pitfalls.

g.text: The wishlist waits on 4 layer teams for 28 days, the monolith mirrors them, checkout owns too much.
Six stream-aligned teams own their flow; Launchpad, the SRE group and recommendations ease the load.
X-as-a-Service from Launchpad, 6 weeks of SRE facilitating, 3 months of collaboration on ranking.
Launchpad takes checkout's plumbing and payments gets its own team; then four common pitfalls.
THE SYSTEM MIRRORS THEM: CONWAY’S LAW
two domains plus the plumbing: more than
the team can keep in its head
waiting in other teams’ queues 19 d
✓ catalog’s wishlist change: live in 2 days, no handoffs
each owns a slice of the shop
end to end: builds it, runs it,
so no team builds its own
coaches a team until it has
X-as-a-Service: the returns service in staging in 20 min, not 9 working days
SLOs, alerts and on-call in place; the SRE group moves on
X-as-a-Service: API v2 stable, search too
Acme wants payments as its own
so it forms the payments team first;
new names, same 3 handoffs: move the ownership
9 days for a service again: keep it self-service
still pairing at month 9: agree an end and an API
a 15-person team acts as two: aim for 5 to 9 people
